title: The Salt Current
premise: Ada Ashgrove, a desert ranger who has spent a decade erasing himself from every ledger, is hired to track a thief across the salt flats—only to find the trail ends where a government survey team vanished without tracks, leaving behind sealed gear stamped with his own family name. The thief, a woman named Sefi, stole not valuables but the concession permits that will decide who owns the water beneath the flats when the monsoon floods them. Pursuing her through the rising season, Ada discovers his estranged father sold their inherited water rights to the survey consortium before dying, and that staying invisible means letting strangers drown. In the end Ada and Sefi ride out the monsoon in a leaking boat, deliver the permits to expire unclaimed, and Ada chooses belonging over anonymity, claiming the inheritance he spent years running from.
about_author: Isandro Villalobos is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six seasons mapping ephemeral rivers before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that punish anyone who mistakes emptiness for safety.

chapters.title: The Debt of Dry Ground
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A desert ranger takes one last tracking contract: recover stolen documents from a thief named Sefi, payment enough to clear his debts and disappear for good. He reads her trail across hardpan and finds it deliberately, almost respectfully legible. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a man already halfway gone from the world.

chapters.title: Tracks That End Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The trail terminates at a government survey camp—tents standing, kettles cold, gear stacked and sealed, no bodies, no tracks leading out. Among the crates he finds a land grant bearing the Ashgrove name. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as the empty camp mirrors his own chosen emptiness.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Left a Light Burning
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. She watches Ada search the camp through binoculars, having left the trail readable on purpose to draw him in. Flashbacks reveal she stole the permits because the consortium's survey would erase three settlements' claims. Emotional beat: guilt braided with resolve; she needs him whether he knows it or not.

chapters.title: What the Salt Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following a second, stranger trail—drag marks, a dropped instrument—he finds one survivor of the survey team, delirious, muttering about water rising where no water should be. The man dies at dusk. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, and the first crack in Ada's vow of neutrality.

chapters.title: Concession
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. In a canal-town market, Sefi studies the permits: sixty days until they expire unclaimed, after which the water rights revert to the settlements—if no heir contests them. She learns an Ashgrove heir exists. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into strategy, and the burden of using a man as a key.

chapters.title: The Thief Catches the Tracker
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sefi lets Ada corner her in a drying warehouse, then offers a trade: help me reach the registry before monsoon closes the causeways, and I'll show you what your father signed. Emotional beat: wary negotiation between two people who both survive by trusting no one.

chapters.title: A Father's Signature
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reading the deeds aboard Sefi's boat, Ada learns his father sold the family's water rights weeks before dying—and that the survey team's disappearance coincides with the consortium falsifying flow data. Emotional beat: old abandonment wounds reopened; anger redirected from father to system.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They run the falling canals together, trading watch shifts, learning each other's silences. Consortium agents shadow them from the levees. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership warming into something neither will name yet.

chapters.title: The Registry Burns Early
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Arriving at the registry town, they find it ablaze—the consortium destroying records ahead of schedule. Sefi saves a clerk's ledger at the cost of revealing herself. Emotional beat: fury and despair; the legal path is closing faster than planned.

chapters.title: Witnesses in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hiding in the marshes, they encounter survivors of the vanished survey team—not murdered but defected, hiding with evidence of the falsified surveys. Their leader knew Ada's father. Emotional beat: shock of discovery; Ada realizes his father may have died trying to undo the sale.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Comes Down
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The season's first storm hits with biblical force; the marsh becomes open water, the boat springs a leak, and the defectors' camp floods. Everyone piles into one vessel. Emotional beat: terror stripped to essentials—bailing, bailing, bailing—forging the group into something like a crew.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Flats
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Days adrift on flooded salt flats, patching the hull with canvas and pitch, Ada navigates by drowned landmarks only he remembers from childhood. Emotional beat: the desert boy discovering the water is also home; belonging arriving sideways.

chapters.title: What Sefi Stole
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Confession under tarpaulin: Sefi's village was drowned by an earlier 'survey' that rerouted a river; the permits are her revenge and her penance. Ada admits he tracked people for the same consortium once. Emotional beat: mutual absolution neither fully believes yet.

chapters.title: Agents on the Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Consortium boats find them; a running chase through drowned channels costs the defectors their evidence cache. One agent recognizes Ada and offers him his old life back. Emotional beat: temptation made flesh—safety offered at exactly the price of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada turns the offer down publicly, burning his old ranger credentials as signal fire to misdirect the pursuit. The act makes him a target and, finally, a member of the crew. Emotional beat: liberation through self-destruction; invisibility surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: High Water at the Registry Ruins
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Racing the permit deadline, they return to the burned registry, where the surviving clerk has rebuilt a partial record from memory. But filing requires an heir's signature—an Ashgrove must contest the sale in person. Emotional beat: the trap of the premise snapping shut around Ada's name.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reading his father's hidden letter, recovered from the defectors, Ada learns the sale was coerced and the elder Ashgrove died gathering proof. To contest it, Ada must stand in daylight as himself. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the name becomes armor instead of shame.

chapters.title: The Storm That Decides
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The consortium moves to seize the ruins before the filing; the final battle happens in the teeth of the peak monsoon, hull against hull in white water. Sefi is swept overboard. Emotional beat: chaos as crucible; everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Overboard
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada dives into the flood for Sefi, nearly drowning, saved by the very currents his father's maps predicted. They limp back to the ruins as the storm breaks. Emotional beat: love admitted in the space between almost dying and not.

chapters.title: Sixty Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. At the last hour, Ada signs the contest; the permits lapse unclaimed, and the water rights revert to the settlements under settlement law. The consortium's claim collapses for lack of a valid holder. Emotional beat: quiet triumph—victory achieved not by force but by patience and paper.

chapters.title: The Current Runs Both Ways
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Aftermath: the defectors testify, the settlements rebuild, and Ada is offered his father's old post as warden of the restored waterways. He accepts, signing his full name for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: peace earned; power accepted with eyes open to its cost.

chapters.title: Salt and Fresh
chapters.summary: Dual epilogue POV. Months later, Ada and Sefi walk the flats as the flood recedes, mapping the new channels together. Where the salt meets fresh water, life returns first. Emotional beat: belonging as ongoing practice, not destination—a current, not a harbor.
